correctness.rationale: A complete bijection reconstructs every actual bisimulation from compatible pairs of equivalence classes and edge covers in each atomic-profile block, checking both directions of atomic/forth/back. The independent choices yield all-witness counts; a nested inclusion-minimality argument yields the nonempty and global minimal counts. Bipartite edge-cover inclusion-exclusion and star-forest EGF/recurrence are proved from first principles. Boundary cases with no compatibility edges or isolated class vertices are handled. Direct exhaustive enumeration of nonempty relations for all 2500 one-to-three-world model pairs plus four four-versus-three-world cases matches all four formulas; checker output ALL_CHECKS_OK model_pairs=2504 profile_cases=5. Finite tests support but do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The all-size exact four-way census is not supplied by the inspected complete text of the motivating arXiv paper, whose Definition 3 establishes semantic clauses and whose main results concern definability, axiomatization and complexity; nor by the complete author-posted 2014 article, which introduces total bisimulation and establishes its definability. Independent graph edge-cover counts and star components are credited combinatorial ingredients, and related fixed-model quotient and bounded-morphism research concerns different mathematical objects. Nine actual semantic-alias and dominance searches were performed against published research records, with closest claims compared by implications rather than titles. Unsearched or differently indexed literature remains a real priority risk.
residual_risks: An older result indexed under relation coverings, modal equivalence witnesses, or labelled bipartite star forests might imply some or all of the counting theorem; no absolute priority certification is asserted.
The theorem is restricted to finite fixed labelled one-agent S5 models; extension to multimodal S5 or arbitrary frames is not established.

value.rationale: A natural quantitative invariant of finite epistemic-model comparison is the exact number of bisimulation witnesses, especially global and inclusion-minimal ones. Prior cited research primarily proves existence/expressibility; the new classification handles arbitrary world partitions, atomic-color multiplicities and unequal class sizes and gives four explicit all-size counts. The two-level star-forest criterion is a structural lemma needed to enumerate the minimal global witnesses, not a mere fixed small-instance table. It is motivated by witness complexity in model comparison and distinguishes different S5 partitions on the same number of worlds. No general multiagent theorem or unsupported downstream use is claimed.
